title: Imperial Capital Undercurrents
next_chapter_hook: A secret letter from an ally made Chen Ji's pupils constrict sharply—the news that Chen Nian was imprisoned in the Imperial Capital's forbidden grounds was actually an elaborately woven bait.

text.content: The wind and crane cries at the gate finally ceased. Chen Ji stood with hands clasped behind his back by the window, his gaze piercing through the thin silk curtains to fall upon the oil-paper umbrella still left unfolded in the courtyard. The umbrella's surface bore a light ink landscape painting, an imperial object commissioned by the Ministry of Works—no ordinary noble had the right to use it. Only the dragon's sons and phoenix's grandchildren could bear such an umbrella into the inner city. The Crown Prince had come personally, and this move had landed precisely at the center of Chen Ji's chessboard.

dialogue.content: (Fingers tapping lightly on the window lattice, voice languid) To open, or not to open... that is the question.

text.content: The Tianji Record Fragment stirred with faint light in the Mental Sea. Chen Ji reached out with his consciousness to touch that blurred thread of prophecy—the next three hours' trajectory surfaced in his heart: the consequences of opening the door were clear, as were those of keeping it shut. He wanted to see both futures clearly. The fragment trembled, and countless images flickered past like a carousel. His brow gradually knit tight—within the Crown Prince's shadow, there was actually a thread he had not noticed before.

dialogue.content: (Emerging from behind the screen, voice pressed extremely low) He has been standing outside for half an hour already.

(Turning around, gaze tranquil as still water) Not just half an hour. His patience exceeds my expectations. Junior Sister Su, do you know of any unusual disturbances at the Crown Prince's residence recently?
(Brow slightly creasing) I've discovered something... strange. The Crown Prince's household expenses have tripled in the past three months, yet he clearly receives no imperial favor.

text.content: Upon hearing this, the corner of Chen Ji's lips lifted slightly. Expenses tripled yet no imperial favor? Where was the silver coming from? The answer was obvious—someone was secretly funneling resources, and that someone hid so deeply even the imperial intelligence agents couldn't trace them. He traced the Crown Prince's life thread once more with the Tianji Record. This time, that hidden line finally revealed its true form—it was actually an old eunuch who had long been officially 'dead' in the palace.

dialogue.content: (A low laugh, the smile not reaching his eyes) Interesting... the Crown Prince is a puppet, the true mastermind lies elsewhere.
(Expression slightly shifting) Are you saying... the legendary 'Shadow Chancellor' within the palace?

(Nodding) The chief writing eunuch who served beside the late Emperor, attending to three generations of sovereigns. Twenty years ago, he was declared deceased, but in truth, he has remained hidden all along. This person is the true Chess Player of this entire game.

text.content: Su Qingyao drew a sharp breath. The chief writing eunuch controlled imperial seals and military command tokens—without the title of prime minister, yet possessing all its power. When the late Emperor passed, it was said he personally arranged the current Emperor's succession—if this person still manipulates from the shadows, then how much of the imperial edicts from the capital truly originate from the Son of Heaven's will? Chen Ji, however, wore his usual expression, as if this information had long been within his expectations.

choice.prompt: The situation had become clear, but how should the path forward be traversed? The Crown Prince delivering himself to his doorstep was both opportunity and trap.

choices.text: Leverage: Open the Door and Receive the Guest
choices.description: Exploit the Crown Prince's desperation for aid to extract more intelligence about the 'Shadow Chancellor' from him.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain Core Intelligence of the Dynasty
choices.risk_hint: The Crown Prince May See Through the Disguise

text.content: Chen Ji straightened his gray robe of a menial servant, concealing all sharpness to its deepest recesses, and slowly walked toward the courtyard gate. The wooden door creaked open, revealing the young prince outside. Clearly, he hadn't expected Chen Ji to personally answer the door. A flash of astonishment crossed his eyes—quickly replaced by deeper anxiety.

choices.text: Divide and Conquer: First Probe the Princess
choices.description: The Crown Prince poses no threat; the Princess is the variable. Before responding to the Crown Prince, first ascertain Hua'an Princess's full hand.
choices.visible_cost: May Miss Intelligence Offered by the Crown Prince
choices.risk_hint: The Crown Prince May Seek Other Avenues

text.content: Chen Ji did not walk toward the courtyard gate. Instead, he turned and retrieved a command token from the Hidden Compartment, handing it to Su Qingyao. Go, deliver this token to Hua'an Princess's residence. Say simply... an old friend sends regards. Su Qingyao took the token, wanting to speak yet ultimately asking nothing, and vanished into the night.

Whether opening the door or not, the Crown Prince had waited too long outside the courtyard. Chen Ji ordered tea and refreshments sent up, while he himself sat leisurely in the side hall, sipping tea with unhurried composure. Through the gap in the window lattice, he watched the Crown Prince's expression shift from anticipation to agitation, then from agitation to an indescribable fear. That expression... interesting.

After Su Qingyao left, Chen Ji sat alone in the study, fingertips unconsciously stroking the edge of the Tianji Record Fragment. The Princess's life thread was equally obscure and difficult to decipher—an extremely rare occurrence in his divinations. An ordinary person's future appeared before him like an open book. Only those whose fates intertwined deeply with the Heavenly Will would present this mist-like chaos. Hua'an Princess was by no means as simple as she appeared.

dialogue.content: (Eyes flickering slightly) She is not waiting for the opportune moment... she herself is the opportunity.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao sent back word that Hua'an Princess had actually come out personally to greet her—was this a gesture of goodwill, or a probe?

choices.description: Meet the Princess as Chen Ji's former subordinate, getting straight to the point about her true intentions.

text.content: Chen Ji changed into a plain white robe and went alone to where the Princess's carriage waited. Hua'an Princess sat behind the pearl curtain, her otherworldly beauty visible through the translucent fabric, yet her tone was cold as frost: 'Are you Chen Ji's person?'

choices.description: Have Su Qingyao appear on his behalf while he observes the Princess's reactions from the shadows, discerning the细微 from the obvious.

text.content: Chen Ji did not show himself. Instead, he hid in the shadows, using the Tianji Record to capture the subtle fluctuations in the Princess's emotions. The woman behind the pearl curtain seemed to have anticipated this scene long ago, her lips curving into a meaningful arc: 'Chen Ji... interesting.'

Whether Crown Prince or Princess, the waters of the Imperial Capital ran deeper than he imagined. Chen Ji sorted through the intelligence in his mind: the Crown Prince had the 'Shadow Chancellor' pulling his strings, the Princess feigned neutrality while harboring ambitions, and beyond these two forces, countless undercurrents surged—agents of various Sects in the dynasty, eyes of regional princes, and that Heavenly Will forever looming over everything. Each step he took was like walking on thin ice.

dialogue.content: (Eyes closed, focusing his mind) The Imperial Capital is one grand chess game. What I need is not merely chess pieces... I need cards that can turn the tables.

text.content: Deep night, a secret letter arrived at Chen Ji's desk. He unfolded the Letter, and his gaze suddenly froze—the matters described in the letter coincided perfectly with the leads he had been investigating: Chen Nian had indeed been brought into the Imperial Capital, and the place of imprisonment was precisely that legendary Imperial Capital Forbidden Grounds. Yet, a sentence at the letter's end made his pupils constrict sharply. 'This information's source is questionable—may be a trap. Exercise caution.'

choice.prompt: The news about Chen Nian may be a trap, but would Chen Ji let slip any lead concerning his sister?

choices.description: Knowing it's a trap, he must walk into it—but make the trap-setter become the mantis stalked by the oriole.
choices.visible_cost: Consume Heavenly Fate to Divine the Full Picture of the Trap
choices.visible_reward: Counter-attack, exposing the mastermind behind the scenes
choices.risk_hint: The Forbidden Grounds Are Extremely Dangerous

text.content: Chen Ji burned the Letter, a resolute flash crossing his eyes. Whoever dared to use Chen Nian as bait... he would teach them what it meant to have schemes within schemes. In the wavering candlelight, his shadow cast upon the wall like a dormant beast slowly opening its eyes.

choices.description: Stay put, first use other pieces to probe the trap's depth, preserving strength.
choices.risk_hint: The Sister May Be in Danger

text.content: Chen Ji placed the Letter into the Hidden Compartment, his expression returning to calm. Chen Nian... he had searched for five years; he could wait a while longer. But if this trap truly involved her, he would make the trap-setter pay ten times the price. The night wind outside the window howled mournfully, as if whispering some unknown secret.

Night dyed the world in ink, and the Imperial Capital's hustle gradually quieted. Chen Ji sat alone by the window, his gaze turned toward the direction of the palace. There, lights blazed—the Hall of Diligent Governance where the Son of Heaven handled state affairs—or perhaps the secret command center of the 'Shadow Chancellor' lurking in the shadows? He gently closed his eyes. The ink characters on the Tianji Record Fragment faintly glowed, as if narrating some ancient and cruel truth. This game has only just begun.

dialogue.content: (The remnant soul's voice drifting悠悠响起) The waters of the Imperial Capital run deeper than you imagine... the Shadow Chancellor is merely another's chess piece.

text.content: Chen Ji's eyes snapped open. Master Mo's words were like a basin of cold water, splashing over the chessboard he had just begun to sort out. The Shadow Chancellor is a chess piece? Then who is the Chess Player? He raised his head toward the waning moon in the night sky, half-obscured by dark clouds, and an unprecedented chill surged in his heart. The shadow of the Eye of Heavenly Fate seemed closer than ever before. The ally's secret letter still gripped in his hand, that final sentence transforming into an invisible thorn, piercing his heart. Chen Nian... wait for me.
